newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says F-16 sale to Taiwan fully legal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says F-16 sale to Taiwan fully legal.

text.p: The United States on Tuesday defended its sale of advanced F-16 fighters to Taiwan as completely legal and Taiwan took delivery of the first two jets.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the sale, which has outraged China, was "fully consistent" with Washington's Taiwan Relations Act and with a U.S.-Chinese joint statement of 1982 on arms sales to Taiwan.
"This sale is for defensive purposes only. It helps to assure the defence needs of Taiwan," Burns told reporters.

Burns confirmed statements by Taiwan that the island had taken delivery Monday of the first two of 150 F-16s ordered from the United States in a deal approved in 1992 by former U.S. President George Bush.
The United States severed diplomatic relations with Taiwan after establishing ties with China in 1979, but maintains an informal relationship.
China, which has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since the two split after a civil war in 1949, vows to retake the island eventually.
